Fast Splash of Colour
At the start of 1985, Toleman found itself without
a tyre deal and was unable to compete in the first
three races of the season. It was only a substantial
financial injection from the fashion brand
Benetton that persuaded Pirelli to supply tyres
from the Monaco GP onwards. This not only saved
the season for Teo Fabi but also enabled Toleman
to field a second car for Piercarlo Ghinzani from
the Austrian Grand Prix.
The TG185, designed by Rory Byrne and powered
by a Hart 4-cylinder turbo engine, was, in combi-
nation with the Pirelli tyres, the big surprise of the
year anyway, even if it took a bit of luck for Teo
Fabi to secure pole position on the new Nürburg-
ring Grand Prix circuit.

Just as unusual as the Italian fashion brand’s
advertising campaigns were in the 1980s, so too
was the Toleman’s livery that year: the national
flags of the world - arranged differently at every
Grand Prix - were spread across the car. A true
splash of colour on the grid. Teo Fabi was the first
to take to the track on Friday and had set a fast
time in dry conditions.
Then the rain came and no one was able to beat
his time. Toleman’s first pole position! However,
after crashing out on Saturday, Fabi started
Sunday’s race from the front row in the spare car.
The clutch promptly failed and the Italian dropped
back to eighth place. It was precisely this compo-
nent that ultimately led to his retirement on lap 29.

The quiet town of Hockenheim in Baden-
Württemberg will once again be trans-
formed into a mecca for German motor
racing fans this weekend. Traditionally,
the DTM season finale takes place here
in October.
This year, too, the two final races promise
to keep spectators on the edge of their
seats right up to the very end. A driver can
still score a maximum of 56 points from
the races and qualifying sessions this
weekend. In theory, based on the current
standings, these 56 points could help six
drivers from five different manufacturers
win the title.
At the top of the championship is the
current leader, Thomas Preining, in the
formidable Manthey Porsche. With 197
points, he is in the best position heading
into the grand finale.
Mercedes driver Maro Engel follows
with 174 points. He has already secured
victory this year in the legendary 24-hour
race at the Nurburgring.
inale
Just one point behind him is Marco
Wittmann, a true DTM professional. In his
‘Green Machine’, he could clinch his third
DTM championship title this weekend.
The fourth in the running is Mercedes
driver Lucas Auer. However, trailing by
45 points, he will need a lot to go his way
if he wants to be in contention at the top
once again.
Matteo Cairoli (Ferrari) and Nicki Thiim
(Aston Martin) are two further potential
title contenders. However, trailing
Preining by 47 and 50 points respec-
tively, it will be difficult for either of
them to make the leap to the top of the
standings.
wOne thing is certain: at Hockenheim,
the title will ultimately be decided in the
final metres!
